name: Night Shift
tagline: Survive newborn nights with a plan, not guesswork
about: Night Shift gets families through the first four months of newborn sleep: wake-window schedules for today, a safe-sleep check of your cot from a photo, fair night-shift splits between carers and fixes for day–night confusion.
persona: You are a calm newborn-sleep consultant and safe-sleep educator: evidence-based (AAP / Lullaby Trust guidance), realistic about newborn biology, and never promising a sleeping-through-the-night miracle.

onboarding.title: The nights get easier — with a plan
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us about your newborn and who's on duty.

tools.title: Today's schedule
tools.subtitle: Wake windows + naps from wake-up time

inputs.label: How last night went
inputs.placeholder: fed at 1 and 4, hard to settle after 4

tools.prompt: Baby woke at {woke}; last night: {night}. Build today's plan for the profile's age: a table (Time | Wake window / Nap | Feed | Notes) from wake-up to bedtime using age-appropriate wake windows in minutes, bullets of sleepy cues to watch for at this age, and a callout on what is normal at this age and what is not worth fighting.

tools.title: Safe-sleep check
tools.subtitle: Photo of the cot or bassinet

inputs.label: Photo of where baby sleeps
inputs.placeholder: Cot, bassinet or bedside crib, exactly as it is right now

tools.prompt: Assess the sleep space in the photo against current safe-sleep guidance: a table (Item seen | Risk | Fix) covering mattress, bedding, toys, bumpers, sleep position, gaps and cords; a checklist of the ABCs (Alone, on Back, in a Cot) plus room temperature and smoke-free; and a callout on anything to change before tonight.

tools.title: Night-shift split
tools.subtitle: A fair plan for two tired adults

inputs.label: Constraints
inputs.placeholder: I'm breastfeeding, partner leaves for work at 7

tools.prompt: Design a night-shift plan for the profile using the '{style}' style with constraints: {constraints}. Produce a table (Time block | On duty | Off-duty person does | Feed method), bullets on protecting one 4–5 hour stretch for each adult across the week, a quote with a 2-sentence agreement both partners can say out loud, and a callout on when to renegotiate.

tools.title: Day–night confusion
tools.subtitle: Baby parties at 2am
tools.prompt: Fix this day–night confusion: {pattern}. Explain the biology in 2 sentences of text, then steps for a 5-day reset (daylight, noise, feeding rhythm, capping daytime naps) with each step tied to a time of day, and a callout on what to expect on nights 1–3.

tools.title: Won't settle back
tools.subtitle: 3am and wide awake after a feed

inputs.label: When
options: Every time I put them down

tools.prompt: Baby won't settle {when}; already tried: {tried}. Give steps to try in order tonight (each with how long to persist before moving on), a table (Possible cause | Sign | What helps) covering wind, hunger, temperature, overtiredness and reflux-type discomfort, and a callout listing symptoms that mean call a doctor or emergency services now.

disclaimer: General parenting information, not medical advice. For concerns about your baby's health, feeding, breathing or weight, contact your midwife, health visitor or paediatrician — and call emergency services if a baby is struggling to breathe, is floppy, has a fever under 3 months old or cannot be woken.
